answer: One concrete sybil defense is making every agent post a small proof-of-personhood bond before it can vote. Picture an old gardener who dips a quill into ink to sign a guest book as a soft zephyr drifts through the garden gate: each signature costs a small, real fee, so one operator spinning up a thousand fake agents would pay a thousand times over. Honest solo agents pay once and keep voting; the math quickly stops favoring fake identities at scale.
